profiles.title: Portable Python agent API
profiles.summary: Hayate has the clearest first-party path when one Python application must run on ASGI, native Cloudflare Workers, and buffered or response-streaming AWS Lambda HTTP payload v2 while combining typed HTTP contracts, cached dependency graphs, MCP 2025-11-25, authorization, and checked SQLite/D1 access.

profiles.title: Conventional typed Python API
profiles.summary: Hayate now meets FastAPI's central typed request/response, OpenAPI, dependency-graph, direct-test, realtime, lifecycle, and sub-application composition capabilities. FastAPI retains a much larger adoption ecosystem; that is a material adoption advantage, not a missing Hayate endpoint feature.

profiles.title: Traditional database-backed full stack
profiles.summary: Django remains functionally ahead for model-driven admin, ORM/migrations, and integrated forms/templates. Hayate offers composable checked SQL and htmx paths, and can now retain a Django admin/ORM application under an ASGI prefix during incremental migration instead of reproducing Django's monolith.

profiles.title: JavaScript and TypeScript edge application
profiles.summary: Hono remains functionally ahead for multi-JavaScript-runtime reach and route-inferred TypeScript RPC, and its JavaScript Workers runtime has materially better startup, memory, CPU, and upload size than Python Workers.

capabilities.title: Web-standard Fetch core
capabilities.definition: Application handlers use standard Request/Response/URL/Headers concepts rather than a Python-only server protocol.

hayate.note: Fetch-shaped request/response core with ASGI and Workers as adapters.

fastapi.note: The documented application model is Starlette on ASGI, not a Fetch core.

django.note: Django documents its own HttpRequest/HttpResponse stack over WSGI or ASGI.

hono.note: Hono explicitly uses Web Standards and the Fetch API.

capabilities.title: ASGI server compatibility
capabilities.definition: The application can run behind ordinary Python ASGI servers.

hayate.note: Hayate is directly ASGI-callable and validates HTTP, WebSocket, lifespan, and background work.

fastapi.note: FastAPI is an ASGI framework built on Starlette.

django.note: Django documents an async request stack under ASGI.

hono.note: Hono targets JavaScript runtimes and their adapters rather than Python ASGI.

capabilities.title: Independent sub-application composition
capabilities.definition: An application can dispatch an independent framework application under a path prefix with correct sub-application path semantics.

hayate.note: ASGIPathDispatcher mounts Django, FastAPI, or another ASGI application by longest prefix while keeping the Fetch core and Workers adapter unchanged.

fastapi.note: FastAPI mounts independent sub-applications with their own routes, OpenAPI, and automatic documentation.

django.note: Django can be embedded in an outer ASGI composition, but its documented core does not provide a path dispatcher for independent applications.

hono.note: Hono route() composes Hono applications and mount() integrates applications from other Fetch frameworks.

capabilities.title: Native Cloudflare Workers path without ASGI
capabilities.definition: The framework connects Fetch requests directly to its application model without an ASGI protocol bridge.

hayate.note: Class and global Python Workers entrypoints convert one Fetch boundary and retain bindings.

fastapi.note: Cloudflare supports FastAPI through its Python Workers ASGI server and asgi.fetch bridge.

django.note: Django documents WSGI/ASGI deployment; no native Fetch adapter is in its framework surface.

hono.note: Cloudflare Workers is a primary Hono runtime and uses app.fetch.

capabilities.title: Native AWS Lambda HTTP and response-streaming path
capabilities.definition: The framework package translates API Gateway HTTP API v2 and Function URL events directly and can incrementally stream responses, without a separately governed ASGI-to-Lambda adapter.

hayate.note: to_lambda maps buffered payload-v2 requests directly to the Fetch core, while run_lambda_streaming implements the custom Runtime API's chunking, HTTP metadata, cookies, and error trailers; CI installs the wheel in AWS's Python image and proves first-chunk delivery on the Runtime API wire.

fastapi.note: FastAPI's deployment documentation delegates other cloud providers to provider guides; the framework package does not include an AWS Lambda event adapter.

django.note: Django documents WSGI and ASGI deployment and ASGI servers, not a first-party API Gateway or Function URL event adapter.

hono.note: hono/aws-lambda supplies maintained buffered and response-streaming Lambda handlers.

capabilities.title: Typed request and response OpenAPI contracts
capabilities.definition: Types drive input validation, response validation/serialization, OpenAPI 3.1, interactive docs, and client generation.

hayate.note: hayate-openapi 0.7 provides explicit source markers, portable typed constraints, typed binary files, response contracts, pluggable schema providers, OpenAPI 3.1.1, and Scalar on CPython and Python Workers.

fastapi.note: Type-driven validation, OpenAPI, JSON Schema, and interactive docs are central FastAPI features.

django.note: API schemas and typed REST contracts are provided by projects such as Django REST Framework rather than Django core.

hono.note: @hono/zod-openapi combines validation, types, and OpenAPI generation.

capabilities.title: Resource-bounded multipart file uploads
capabilities.definition: Multipart files can be consumed incrementally with explicit resource limits, bounded memory, deterministic cleanup, and a disk-free edge path.

hayate.note: FormDataLimits caps total body, file, field, part count, and headers; native ASGI parsing streams to a configurable temporary-file threshold while Workers stays bounded without disk, and typed OpenAPI files reuse the same contract.

fastapi.note: UploadFile provides a spooled file, metadata, and async reads; multipart parsing depends on the separately installed python-multipart package.

django.note: Django upload handlers stream incoming data and switch between memory and temporary files, with settings and custom handlers for resource policy.

hono.note: Hono exposes Fetch form parsing and whole-body limit middleware, but framework-level multipart spill, per-file, field, part, and header controls are not part of that documented path.

capabilities.title: Nested dependency graph with request cache
capabilities.definition: Endpoint dependencies may have subdependencies and shared results are cached once per request.

hayate.note: hayate-openapi Depends resolves sync/async subdependencies with per-request caching.

fastapi.note: FastAPI documents arbitrarily deep subdependencies and one-call-per-request caching.

django.note: Django's documented core feature set does not include a general endpoint dependency-injection graph.

hono.note: Hono documents DI options such as Hono Simple DI in its third-party middleware catalog.

capabilities.title: First-party MCP Streamable HTTP
capabilities.definition: The framework organization maintains an MCP transport that mounts into the web app and works on its edge runtime.

hayate.note: hayate-mcp tests MCP 2025-11-25 on ASGI and native Python Workers with the official conformance runner.

fastapi.note: FastAPI-MCP is a separate community project that mounts through ASGI.

django.note: MCP is not part of Django's documented first-party module set.

hono.note: @hono/mcp is maintained in the honojs middleware repository and implements Streamable HTTP.

capabilities.title: OAuth authorization server, resource server, and DPoP
capabilities.definition: One maintained stack supplies authorization-server metadata/endpoints, resource protection, scopes, and proof-of-possession support for agent APIs.

hayate.note: hayate-auth and hayate-mcp share principals, scopes, OAuth metadata, and DPoP verification.

fastapi.note: FastAPI provides OpenAPI-integrated security primitives and tutorials, not a maintained authorization-server product.

django.note: Django core provides user/password/session authentication and permissions, not OAuth AS plus DPoP.

hono.note: Hono ships auth middleware and MCP auth routing helpers, but not the complete authorization-server and DPoP stack.

capabilities.title: One checked SQL contract on SQLite and D1
capabilities.definition: The same SQL declarations are cardinality-checked and generate typed Python calls for local SQLite and Cloudflare D1.

hayate.note: hayate-sql plus the golden app compile one migration/query set and execute it on SQLite and real D1.

fastapi.note: FastAPI is database-agnostic and delegates database contracts to external packages.

django.note: Django has a first-party ORM for documented SQL backends, but not a shared SQLite/Cloudflare D1 checked-SQL path.

hono.note: Hono exposes D1 through the runtime; checked SQL/code generation is delegated to database libraries.

capabilities.title: Direct application request testing
capabilities.definition: Tests can call the application without starting a socket server.

hayate.note: app.request executes the Fetch core directly and accepts runtime env bindings.

fastapi.note: FastAPI documents TestClient for direct application tests.

django.note: Django provides synchronous and asynchronous test clients.

hono.note: app.request accepts Request data and optional runtime env values.

capabilities.title: WebSocket, streaming, and SSE
capabilities.definition: The maintained application surface supports bidirectional sockets and incremental HTTP responses.

hayate.note: ASGI and Workers adapters preserve WebSockets, streaming bodies, abort signals, and SSE.

fastapi.note: FastAPI inherits Starlette WebSockets and streaming responses.

django.note: Django supports streaming HTTP, while WebSocket routing is supplied by Django Channels.

hono.note: Hono ships runtime WebSocket helpers and stream/streamSSE helpers.

capabilities.title: Lifecycle and background work
capabilities.definition: The framework exposes startup/shutdown or runtime lifecycle hooks and a supported path for post-response/background work.

hayate.note: ASGI lifespan hooks and c.wait_until map to server draining or Workers ctx.waitUntil.

fastapi.note: FastAPI documents lifespan events and BackgroundTasks.

django.note: Django 6.0 includes async lifecycle support and a Tasks contract, with execution delegated to infrastructure.

hono.note: Hono exposes runtime execution context including waitUntil on Workers.

capabilities.title: Model-driven administrative UI
capabilities.definition: Model metadata produces a maintained internal CRUD administration interface.

hayate.note: Hayate does not currently ship a model-driven admin product.

fastapi.note: An administrative UI is not part of FastAPI's documented core feature set.

django.note: Django's automatic, customizable model admin is enabled by the default project template.

hono.note: A model-driven admin is not part of Hono's documented framework and helper surface.

capabilities.title: Model-driven ORM and migrations
capabilities.definition: Framework models drive relationships, queries, schema migration generation, and migration execution.

hayate.note: Hayate intentionally provides checked SQL rather than a model-driven ORM.

fastapi.note: FastAPI is database-agnostic and its SQL tutorial composes an external model library.

django.note: Django models, QuerySets, relationships, and migration commands are first-party core features.

hono.note: Hono delegates ORM and migrations to runtime-compatible database packages.

capabilities.title: Maintained HTML, forms, and progressive enhancement path
capabilities.definition: The ecosystem supplies server rendering, form handling, validation, and an executable full-stack starter.

hayate.note: hayate-htmx plus create-hayate provide Jinja, CSRF, fragments, SSE, and tested browser flows.

fastapi.note: FastAPI documents Jinja templates through Starlette and the external Jinja package; form parsing is supported.

django.note: Django includes templates, forms, validation, generic editing views, messages, and CSRF integration.

hono.note: Hono includes JSX/html helpers and validators across form and request sources.

capabilities.title: Multi-JavaScript-runtime portability
capabilities.definition: The same application runs across Workers, Deno, Bun, Node.js, Fastly, Lambda, and other Fetch runtimes.

hayate.note: Hayate targets Python runtimes rather than JavaScript runtimes.

fastapi.note: FastAPI targets Python ASGI runtimes.

django.note: Django targets Python WSGI and ASGI runtimes.

hono.note: Hono documents one Web-standards application across a broad JavaScript runtime set.

capabilities.title: Maintained typed client path
capabilities.definition: Server contracts produce a supported TypeScript client or types without manually duplicating request/response shapes.

hayate.note: create-hayate pins OpenAPI TypeScript generation and checks generated artifacts.

fastapi.note: OpenAPI is built in and the documentation describes automatic client generation.

django.note: Typed API client generation depends on an external schema stack.

hono.note: Hono RPC infers input and output types directly from the chained route type.

capabilities.title: Maintained production scaffold
capabilities.definition: The framework project maintains a generator or template with runnable tests and production-oriented configuration.

hayate.note: create-hayate composes API, Workers, MCP, auth, SQL, OpenAPI, and htmx profiles and validates generated applications.

fastapi.note: The FastAPI organization maintains a full-stack production template.

django.note: django-admin startproject/startapp generate the standard project and application structure.

hono.note: create-hono generates runtime-specific starters.
